deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of §4 ('Schöpfung der irrationalen Zahlen') and the start of §5 ('Ungleichheiten') of Dedekind's theory of real numbers by cuts. It is close to, but not identical with, the printed 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen' (1872). The previous page defined a cut (A1, A2) of Q, showed that {x : x ≤ 0 or x^2 < 2} | {x > 0 : x^2 > 2} is not produced by any rational, and stipulated that each such cut creates a new irrational number α.

(1) Main text, top. The irrational α is regarded as completely defined by its cut. We say α 'corresponds to' or 'produces' the cut. So every cut corresponds to exactly one number, rational or irrational. Two numbers are different iff their cuts are 'essentially different' (wesentlich verschieden; the word was inserted).

(2) Marginal remark (right column, boxed). The uniqueness claim is 'nicht ganz allgemein!'. A rational a produces two cuts, ({x<a}, {x≥a}) and ({x≤a}, {x>a}), because a itself may be put in either class. These two cuts are declared not essentially different. Alternatively one may normalise: a always goes to the second class. Then no cut has a greatest element in its first class.

(3) Further marginal notes (top right):
- For rational cuts one can fix that a belongs to A2.
- A1 is downward closed: a1 ∈ A1 and x < a1 imply x ∈ A1.
- A2 is upward closed.
- One class determines the cut, since A2 = Q \ A1.
- A number is known when its cut is known.

(4) Definition of order. Let α produce (A1, A2) and β produce (B1, B2), with the two cuts essentially different. Then α < β :⇔ A1 ⊆ B1. If A1 ⊄ B1, then α > β. In modern terms this is the inclusion order on lower sets, as in Rudin.

(5) Theorem: α < β ⇒ β > α, and α > β ⇒ β < α.

Proof, first half. Suppose A1 ⊆ B1. If also B1 ⊆ A1, then A1 = B1 and the cuts would be identical, contrary to hypothesis. Hence B1 ⊄ A1, which by definition means β > α.

Proof, second half (begun here, finished on p. 12). Suppose A1 ⊄ B1. Then there is a1' ∈ A1 \ B1, so a1' ∈ B2. Every b1 is smaller than every b2, so b1 < a1'. Since A1 is downward closed (Dedekind: 'because every a2 > a1''), each b1 lies in A1. Thus B1 ⊆ A1, i.e. β < α.

(6) Bottom right. Heading '§5. Ungleichheiten' with the notation: cuts (A1, A2) by α and (B1, B2) by β.
errors: No mathematical error. One unstated point: when cuts are only taken up to the rational-boundary ambiguity, the definition A1 ⊆ B1 must be independent of the representative chosen. It is, for essentially different cuts. Dedekind does not check this here; the marginal normalisation (a always in the second class) removes the issue.

In the first half of the proof, 'weil sonst die beiden Schnitte identisch wären' strictly needs 'essentially identical'. Without normalisation, A1 = B1 forces A2 = B2, so the cuts are literally identical and the argument is fine.

The proof of the second half relies on downward closure of A1. That property is stated only in the marginal note, not in the main-text definition of a cut. The proof is valid since closure follows from every a1 < every a2.

results.what: Real numbers identified with Dedekind cuts of Q; equality as 'not essentially different' cuts; normalisation that the rational boundary goes to the upper class
Order on cuts defined by inclusion of lower classes, A1 ⊆ B1, with proof of the asymmetry/duality α<β ⇔ β>α
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind 1872 (the printed version phrases it via a rational in A1 ∩ B2); the inclusion formulation is textbook-standard (e.g., Rudin)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the well-known Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen (1872), §§4–5. The only minor points of interest are draft variants: order is defined by inclusion of lower classes, and there is an explicit marginal normalisation of rational cuts. Neither is significant beyond textual history.

checkable.asserts: 7/5 lies in A1 of the √2-cut and in B1 of the 3/2-cut, consistent with √2 < 3/2 via A1 ⊆ B1.
3/2 lies in the upper class A2 of the √2-cut, so B1 ⊄ A1, i.e. 3/2 > √2 by the definition.
Consistency of the cut order with the usual order in the example.

transcription_corrections: The left-margin fragments ('-2', '-2', '2)', '+a1²)') are bleed-through or remnants from the facing page. They are not part of this page's text.
'Werden alle rationalen Zahlen ... zerschnitten, und sind diese beiden Schnitte wesentlich verschieden.' is a single conditional sentence ending with a period; the transcription is acceptable.

In the boxed marginal note, the end reads roughly 'bei welchem unter den Zahlen der ersten Klasse eine größte ist' with 'die' inserted above. The trailing 'b' in the right margin is uncertain and probably not a variable.
The second marginal paragraph should read: 'Ist a1 eine Zahl der ersten Klasse, so sind auch alle kleineren Zahlen als a1 in der ersten Klasse enthalten.' (subscript on a1 confirmed).
